Create a new photorealistic image (text-to-image). VISUAL BRAND STYLE (apply strictly):

Brand: PourCanvas, a US homeowner guide to decorative outdoor concrete (driveways, patios, walkways). Every image must read as a real contractor or architectural photograph of an ordinary, well-kept American home, never a CGI render.

- COMPOSITION: use the framing the subject asks for. Default: wide establishing shot at eye level, the concrete surface in the lower half of the frame and the home exterior in the upper half. Close-up and detail shots make the surface texture, joints and edges the subject; the home is then secondary or absent.
- CAMERA: eye level, 28 mm equivalent unless the subject says otherwise. Deep depth of field, sharp from the foreground surface to the roofline. No fisheye or exaggerated wide-angle distortion. Fine natural grain, no HDR look, no AI sheen.
- LIGHT: natural daylight with true color. Soft pre-peak afternoon sun or bright diffuse overcast. No dramatic golden-hour flare, no lens flare, no flat grey underexposure.
- SURFACE REALISM (most important): the concrete is one to two seasons old, not showroom-new. Subtle tonal variation across the slab, slight darkening at control joints and edges, faint soft efflorescence patches, a faint traffic-wear path along the natural driving or walking line. Control joints and edges are crisp and plausible. Material detail where it applies: broom finish shows slight brush-pressure variation; stamped concrete shows relief depth and darker release color in the recesses; exposed aggregate shows varied pebble density; integral color shows gentle mottling, never a painted plastic look.
- STAGING: the home is lived in, not staged. A vehicle named in the subject sits in the midground at a front three-quarter angle or side-on, never square-on from the rear, and no license plate is visible or legible.
